content.topic: Cardiac troponin assays and diagnostic use
content.summary: Advances in technology have refined cardiac troponin (cTn) assays, particularly high-sensitivity assays (hs-cTn), improving accuracy for detecting and quantifying cardiomyocyte injury and increasing diagnostic accuracy for myocardial infarction (MI) at presentation. hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI assays provide comparable early diagnostic accuracy. The terms 'non-elevated' and 'elevated' (relative to the 99th percentile) are preferred to 'normal'/'abnormal'. Central laboratory high-sensitivity assays are recommended over lower-sensitivity assays; point-of-care (POC) tests have shorter turnaround but lower sensitivity and accuracy. Confounders of hs-cTn concentration include age and renal dysfunction; cTn elevations may occur in clinical conditions other than Type 1 MI.
key_points: hs-cTn assays improve diagnostic accuracy for MI, especially early after chest pain onset.
hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI subunit assays appear comparable in early MI diagnosis.
Avoid 'normal/abnormal' to describe hs-cTn; use 'non-elevated/elevated' with 99th percentile cutoff.
Central laboratory high-sensitivity assays preferred; most POC tests are not high-sensitivity.
POC testing offers shorter turnaround but lower sensitivity, diagnostic accuracy, and NPV.
Confounders affecting hs-cTn: age (very young vs very old), renal dysfunction, and other clinical conditions besides Type 1 MI.
recommendations: Prefer high-sensitivity central laboratory cTn assays over lower-sensitivity assays for diagnostic accuracy.
When reporting hs-cTn, use 'non-elevated' or 'elevated' relative to the 99th percentile.
Be aware of non-MI causes of cTn elevation and adjust interpretation for confounders (age, renal function).
Re-evaluate preference as more validated high-sensitivity POC tests become available.
content.references_in_page: Multiple cited studies and supplementary tables/sections (e.g., Supplementary data online, Table S2, Section 3.3.1, Table S3) supporting statements about hs-cTn performance and clinical implications.
